title: Sparklines + Thresholded Bucket Chart Specs for Per-Model & Per-Route Dashboards
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design ticket to define a set of compact visual components for the Per-Model and Per-Route performance dashboards. Focus is on: (1) micro-sparklines for long-running trends, (2) thresholded bucket histograms for latency and token-size distributions, and (3) an overlaid cost-per-token sparkline for quick economic signal. Components should scale to grids of models/routes, be readable at small sizes, and provide a clear interaction pattern for drilldowns and time-range linking.
goals: Provide a concise at-a-glance row for each model/route showing trend, distribution, and cost
Surface tail latency and token distribution anomalies without occupying full chart real-estate
Enable fast comparison between two selected models/routes and a baseline (e.g., last 24h vs last 7d)
Define interaction patterns for zoom, tooltip detail, and launch-to-detailed-insights page
chart_spec_overview: Sparkline: single-line trend with shaded rolling average (window 1h for hourly resolutions). Show tiny dot marker for latest datapoint and red marker for SLA breaches.

Bucketed histogram: logarithmic bucket boundaries for latency (ms) and token count (tokens). Bins labeled with percent contribution (eg. 65% in 0-20ms). Bars colored by threshold band (good/warn/fail).
Latency envelope: thin band showing p50-p95 and an overlaid p99 marker. Envelope fills use low-opacity brand color.
Cost overlay: secondary y-axis mini-sparkline showing cost-per-1k-tokens normalized; optional toggle to hide for space-constrained views.
Throughput sparkline: stacked micro-area showing requests/sec and tokens/sec compacted into one glyph for each row.
Heat indicator: small square showing recent anomaly score (0-100) derived from evaluation pipeline; click to open anomaly timeline.
Compare mode: when two items selected, sparklines turn into side-by-side normalized lines and bucket histograms become overlaid translucent bars for visual diff.
visual_tokens_and_sizes: Sparkline canvas: 120px width x 24px height (compact) or 180px x 30px
Bucket histogram canvas: 140px x 28px compressed or 220px x 40px expanded
Latency envelope thickness: 2px line for median, 1px dashed for p99 marker
Color tokens: success #0BB85C, warn #FFA94D, fail #FF5C5C, neutral line #374151, baseline #6B7280
interactions: Hover: tooltip shows exact metrics for the hovered timestamp (p50/p95/p99, requests, tokens, cost, sample request id)
Click sparkline: open the detailed model route page anchored to the clicked timestamp and pre-filtered time range (±15min by default)
Shift+click two rows: enter compare mode, persist selection until cleared
Keyboard: focusable rows with Enter to drill in, Space to toggle compare selection
Context menu: quick actions (open logs, open recent PR, start rollout, mute alerts)
Time-range brushing: drawing a range on any sparkline highlights same range across the dashboard grid
acceptance_criteria: Small multiple grid demonstrates readability at 12 rows without horizontal scroll at typical 1366px width
Latency bucket histograms correctly occupy logarithmic bins and color by threshold bands according to SLO config
Hover tooltips show sample request id and link to request tracer when available
Compare mode renders normalized lines and overlaid histograms with clear legend and percent-delta labels
Design tokens and spacing documented so frontend implementers can reproduce two density variants
mocks_review_comments: PM Samir: prefer percent-delta label on hover for quick cost comparisons
Eng Lina: confirm binning math for log buckets and ensure p99 marker can be sourced from aggregated pipeline
SRE Jordan: request sample id in tooltip should link into distributed tracer with autopopulated trace context
Accessibility review: need high-contrast color palette alternate for dark mode and patterns for color-blind users
decisions: Use logarithmic buckets for latency to surface tail behavior across models with different baselines
Show cost overlay off by default to preserve cognitive load; allow toggle per-user
Compact row height default is 48px to support high cardinality grids; comfortable 64px is opt-in via user preference
open_questions: Which alert thresholds map to warn vs fail coloring by default, and should customers be able to supply custom bands?
How should tokenization differences between models be normalized in cost-per-token overlays?
Do we include GPU utilization in the compact row or reserve for detailed view?
next_steps: Incorporate eng feedback on log-bucket implementation and update spec to include exact bucket boundaries
Prototype a11y color variants and run quick contrast checks
Handoff meeting with frontend on 2026-03-05: walk through interactions and provide token JSON
PM to field decision on custom thresholding by 2026-03-09
